task: Review backend robustness, input validation, database exceptions, restart and disaster recovery
scope: Current shared working tree. Source review and isolated fault tests; no runtime fixes or deployment.

findings.title: Numeric overflow escapes validation and lets optional ghosts block valid race acceptance
findings.trigger: A finite JSON integer such as 10**400 in a movement sample or optional ghost pose.
findings.observed: Legacy proof upload returns plain HTTP 500 without X-Request-ID. A trajectory accepted by the actual Python checker fails three worker attempts as verifier_unavailable when the optional ghost contains that integer; identical trajectory without the ghost verifies.
findings.impact: Malformed application data is misclassified as infrastructure failure. Optional presentation can prevent a valid competitive result, contrary to the trajectory-only invariant.
findings.fix: Validate integer magnitude before conversion-dependent finite checks, normalize validation exceptions, and isolate all invalid optional ghost data from score acceptance.
findings.limits: Actual Python checker and HTTP/worker paths; synthetic prepared geometry and fixture manifest. No canonical Godot process was executed.

findings.title: Run retry and successful finalization use opposite row-lock orders
findings.trigger: Retry acquires Player then waits for Run while successful finalization holds Run then requests Player.
findings.observed: A barrier-controlled interleaving on the real disposable PostgreSQL database produced SQLSTATE 40P01 and an HTTP 503 retry response.
findings.impact: A retry racing with result completion can abort either transaction and delay a verified result. Existing durable evidence and cached finalization reduce data-loss risk, but do not remove the deadlock.
findings.fix: Use one consistent Player/Run lock order across API and worker writers; keep finalization fencing and atomic scoring.
findings.limits: The scheduling barrier deliberately makes the supported interleaving deterministic; normal incidence was not measured.

findings.title: Publication retry does not persist or return idempotency receipts
findings.trigger: Repeat the same publication retry key after its first retried verification has failed.
findings.observed: Both requests requeue the intent and reset attempts to zero. No IdempotencyRecord is saved for the retry key; the replay_response return value is ignored.
findings.impact: Lost replies and reconnect/reboot retries can repeat work and reset the retry budget. Reusing a key for another publication is not bound to the original target.
findings.fix: Persist the retry response atomically, return an existing receipt, and bind its scope/body to publication_id.

findings.title: Local object archives and restores do not validate content-addressed integrity
findings.trigger: An existing local blob has corrupted bytes under its original SHA256 filename.
findings.observed: Both archive and restore subprocesses exit zero. The restored object fails LocalBlobStore.get_json integrity checks. Provider archives do call verified get_json; the local branch does not.
findings.impact: The backup wrapper can mark an internally corrupt archive complete. Archive checksums protect transfer of those bytes, not their agreement with the database's content hashes.
findings.fix: Verify bounded decompressed JSON and SHA256 identity during local archive/restore, fail before completion, and validate referenced objects during restore drills.
findings.limits: Actual local archive/restore subprocesses. No production backup or restore was run.

findings.title: Interrupted local uploads leave temporary files that startup and retention never reclaim
findings.trigger: Abrupt process exit after temporary blob bytes have been flushed, before final-name publication.
findings.observed: A real subprocess exited at that point. Its .pending-* file survived a new store initialization and online retention even after its timestamp was moved back 100 days.
findings.impact: Repeated crashes/reboots can accumulate disk usage outside reference-aware object GC and eventually make otherwise valid writes fail for lack of space.
findings.fix: Add bounded conservative cleanup for abandoned temporary files while preserving active uploads and final immutable objects.
findings.limits: Abrupt process exit and initialization were tested; an OS reboot or physical power-loss durability drill was not.

findings.title: S3 streaming errors bypass storage-failure normalization
findings.trigger: response.raw.read raises an urllib3 stream timeout or connection/protocol error after response headers.
findings.observed: Injected urllib3 ReadTimeoutError escapes S3BlobStore instead of becoming OSError. The API's STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE/503 handler therefore does not handle this path. GCS already catches urllib3 HTTPError.
findings.impact: An ordinary S3 transport failure becomes an unstructured 500 and misses the storage-specific readiness invalidation and retry contract.
findings.fix: Normalize raw stream exceptions consistently with the GCS adapter and preserve credential-safe errors.
findings.limits: Injected transport failure; no S3 provider was contacted.

strengths: Ingress bounds wire and decompressed bytes, rejects duplicate JSON keys/nonfinite float values and invalid Unicode, limits JSON nesting, and holds upload slots through handler lifetime.
Sessions close failed transactions; PostgreSQL pools use pre-ping and bounded connection, pool, statement, lock and idle-transaction timeouts.
Acknowledgements follow commits; run submission, refresh recovery and wallet operations retain durable identity and retry protection.

Worker claims use durable leases and fencing. Real PostgreSQL tests passed SQL finalization recovery, interrupted verification/rivalry recovery, concurrent refresh recovery, and mutually exclusive submit/abandon.
Readiness and process liveness are separate and dependency waits coalesce with bounded HTTP deadlines.
Current explicit publication, real worker process kill, replacement worker and exactly one personal best succeeded on SQLite and PostgreSQL with intentionally accelerated lease expiry.
additional_observations: The SQLAlchemyError handler safely hides database details but does not log the exception class/SQLSTATE. Add redacted cause diagnostics linked to request_id; never log SQL parameters or credentials.

Backup guards intentionally require manual recovery after a crash. Full host reboot, physical power loss, NAS storage guarantees, live managed-database failover and production restore acceptance remain untested.

tests.diagnostic_meaning: Eleven passing diagnostics assert reproduction of the six current defects; two additional passing process tests assert successful killed-worker recovery. Passing defect probes do not mean the defects were fixed.

existing_failures.assessment: Assertion predates the two new publication-reference queries. The implementation remains bounded; this is stale coverage, not proof of unbounded retention.

The process fixture still bootstraps through retired remote-draft authoring. Other legacy-bootstrap replica and POSIX worker tests need a current publication setup before those recovery paths are covered reliably. No original assertion was changed.
